pages.text: A gentle spring breeze blew. Dad gave Dodo and Mumu a handful of sunflower seeds each.
"I want to plant them by the field. Then we'll have a sunflower path in summer!" Mumu held the seeds tight.
Dodo shook her seeds. "Scatter them all at once, and they make a forest. I know!"
She scattered her seeds over the soil.
Chirp, chirp! Sparrows flocked down and pecked up her seeds.
"No! Those seeds are for a forest!" Dodo waved her wings.
Only when they were full did the sparrows fly away. Dodo's patch was bare soil.
Mumu planted one seed at a time. Poke—in goes the seed. Pat—a soil blanket on top.
Mumu watered them with a watering can. Little soil mounds stood in a row.
Dodo came holding one last seed safely between both wings. "I won't give you this!" Then, like Mumu, poke—in went the seed. Pat—a soil blanket on top.
